model_metadata:
### Source raw.raw_orders
Table: "ecommerce"."raw"."raw_orders"
Description: One row per order placed in the web shop.
Freshness: measured on `loaded_at`; warn after 6 hours, error after 12 hours
Columns (name · type in warehouse · description):
- order_id · INTEGER · Shop primary key of the order (integer).
- customer_id · INTEGER · CRM customer_id of the customer who placed the order.
- order_date · DATE · Date the order was placed (ISO format YYYY-MM-DD).
- status · VARCHAR · Order lifecycle status: placed, shipped, completed or cancelled.
- loaded_at · TIMESTAMP · UTC timestamp when the ingestion job wrote the row.
lineage:
DAG edges (upstream → downstream; tests omitted):
- source raw.raw_orders → model stg_orders
- model dim_customers → exposure finance_revenue_dashboard
- model dim_customers → exposure marketing_customer_dashboard
- model fct_orders → exposure finance_revenue_dashboard
- model stg_orders → model dim_customers
- model stg_orders → model fct_orders
Downstream nodes (affected if the failing node is wrong or skipped):
- model stg_orders (view): Cleaned orders, one row per order. Expected volume is 500-1,000 orders over the 180-day window.
- model dim_customers (table): One row per customer with order history and lifetime value. Used by marketing and finance dashboards.
- model fct_orders (table): One row per order with payment amounts pivoted by method. Grain must match stg_orders (one row per order).
- exposure finance_revenue_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Finance analytics): Daily revenue by payment method and order status. Refreshed at 07:00 UTC and used in the daily finance stand-up.
- exposure marketing_customer_dashboard (dashboard, owner: Marketing analytics): Customer counts, lifetime value and repeat-purchase rate by country.
Column-level lineage (as designed):
- stg_orders.{order_id, customer_id, status, loaded_at} ← raw_orders (same names)
- stg_orders.order_date ← raw_orders.order_date (cast to date)
- dim_customers.{customer_id, first_name, last_name, email, country_code, created_at} ← stg_customers (same names)
- dim_customers.{first_order_date, most_recent_order_date, number_of_orders} ← stg_orders.order_date / order_id, per customer_id
- dim_customers.lifetime_value ← stg_payments.amount joined via stg_orders.order_id, non-cancelled orders, per customer_id
- fct_orders.{order_id, customer_id, order_date, status} ← stg_orders (same names)
- fct_orders.{credit_card_amount, bank_transfer_amount, voucher_amount, gift_card_amount} ← stg_payments.amount by payment_method, per order_id
- fct_orders.amount ← stg_payments.amount, total per order_id

Recent changes (newest first):
- 2026-10-11 · deploy · Ingestion: orders loader upgraded to v2.3 (watermark-based incremental extraction).
- 2026-10-04 · commit f9bf287 · docs: add column descriptions to models/marts/schema.yml (no SQL change)
- 2026-09-30 · deploy · CRM connector upgraded 3.1 → 3.2 (bug-fix release)
Previous incidents:
- INC-0359 (2026-08-14): orders stale for 14 h while the connector was paused for maintenance. Resolution: connector resumed; missing hours backfilled automatically.
Recent run history:
- raw_orders freshness age at run time, last 7 daily runs: 0.5–1.5 h on previous days; about 30 h today (2026-10-13).
- New rows in raw_orders: normal volume, including 4 rows in the last 30 h.

gold_standard_remediation.root_cause: raw_orders is not really stale. Orders placed in the last 30 h are present (4 rows, latest order_date 2026-10-13), but every one of them has the same loaded_at, 2026-10-12 13:05 UTC, which for some is earlier than when the order was placed. The orders loader upgraded to v2.3 two days ago stamps loaded_at with its extraction watermark, which is stuck, instead of the load time. The freshness check reads loaded_at, so it reports the source as about 30 h stale.
gold_standard_remediation.fix: Ask the ingestion team to fix or roll back loader v2.3 so loaded_at records the actual load time and the watermark advances. Then reload the affected rows so their loaded_at is correct. Do not raise the freshness threshold to make the error go away: a real outage would then go unnoticed.
gold_standard_remediation.verification: `select loaded_at, count(*) from raw.raw_orders group by 1 order by 1 desc limit 5` shows separate hourly load times again, and `dbt source freshness --select source:raw.raw_orders` passes.
